stops.note: 'a little tail, a painter's brush', diminutive of penis 'tail'; also the source of 'pencil'
the botanist Johann Link named this mould genus in 1809 for its brush-like spore stalks

Alexander Fleming noticed in 1928 that a stray mould killed bacteria on a culture plate at St Mary's Hospital, London, and named its active substance in 1929; Howard Florey and Ernst Chain's Oxford team made it a usable drug from 1940

current_meaning: an antibiotic produced from Penicillium moulds
